title: How things work, and the rules
cando: explain how something works, and understand rules and safety notices

about.text: In this lesson you learn how machines work, and the safety rules at work. You listen to a new worker and his supervisor. Then you read a notice and four signs, and show a new colleague a machine.
goals: Explain how something works: If you press this button, the screen comes on.
Ask about a machine: How does it work? What happens if…?
Understand and give rules with must, mustn't, have to, don't have to and allowed to.
Read a machine notice and safety signs, and write five steps with a warning.
Show a new colleague how a machine works and what the safety rules are.

chapters.title: How does it work?
chapters.text:
In this lesson you learn how things work, and the rules at work.
First, you listen to Carlos. It is his first morning at a delivery company.
His supervisor, Mei, gives him a scanner. Carlos asks: How does it work?
Mei says: First, you press this button. Then she explains each step.
Carlos asks: What happens if it doesn't beep? Listen for the answer.
Mei also gives some rules. Listen for mustn't. In mustn't, you don't hear the first t.

chapters.title: If you press this, it starts
chapters.text:
There are two grammar points in this lesson.
One: if, for things that happen every time. If you press this button, the screen comes on.
Use the present in both parts. Do not use will after if.
Two: rules. Must and have to mean: it is necessary. You must wear gloves.
Mustn't and not allowed to mean: don't do it. You mustn't smoke here.
Don't have to is different. It means: it is not necessary, but you can if you want.

chapters.title: A notice and four signs
chapters.text:
Next, you read a notice on a machine in a staff kitchen.
It says how to use the machine, and what can go wrong.
Then you read four safety signs. Signs use very few words. No entry means: you mustn't go in.
Then you write five steps for a machine you know. Start each step with a verb: press, put, wait.
At the end, add one warning with if.

chapters.title: Showing a new colleague
chapters.text:
In the task, you are the expert. A new colleague starts work, and you show them a machine.
Say the steps in order: first, then, after that.
Say what happens if something goes wrong.
Then give the safety rules, with must, mustn't and don't have to.
At the end, check. Ask: Is that clear? Do you want to try?

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a story or an article about how something works, or about rules.
Read it once for the main idea. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: You start a new job. There is a machine you don't know. What do you do first?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. But with a new machine, it is a good idea to ask or read first. Some machines can be dangerous.

conversation.title: Your first scanner
conversation.setting: It is Carlos's first morning at Northgate Deliveries, a warehouse. His supervisor, Mei, gives him the scanner that every driver uses.
lines: Here you are, Carlos. This is your scanner. You use it for every parcel.
Thanks. So how does it work?
First, you press the button on the side. The screen comes on.
You point it at the label and press the yellow button. If it reads the label, it beeps.
What happens if it doesn't beep?
Then you type the number on the screen. It's slower, but it works.
Right. How long does the battery last?
It depends, but usually a whole shift. If the battery is low, the screen goes red.
Am I allowed to take it home and charge it there?
No, you aren't. You have to leave it on the rack by the office every night.
Yes. You mustn't leave it in the van in the sun. It gets hot, and the plastic can melt.
Got it. Press, point, beep, and never in the sun!

questions.q: What happens if the scanner reads the label?
questions.why: Mei says: If it reads the label, it beeps.

questions.q: Where does Carlos leave the scanner every night?
questions.a: on the rack by the office
questions.why: Mei says: You have to leave it on the rack by the office every night.

questions.q: Why mustn't Carlos leave the scanner in the van in the sun?
questions.why: Mei says: It gets hot, and the plastic can melt.

phrases.use: Asking someone to explain a machine.

phrases.text: What happens if it doesn't beep?
phrases.use: Asking about a problem and its result.
Saying the answer is not always the same.

phrases.text: Am I allowed to take it home?
phrases.use: Asking if you can do something.

phrases.text: You mustn't leave it in the sun.
phrases.use: Giving a rule: don't do it.
A short, friendly way to say: I understand.

items.meaning: The part inside a phone or a machine that keeps its power.
items.example: My phone battery lasts all day.

items.meaning: To fill a battery with power again.
items.example: You can charge your phone at your desk.

items.meaning: The part at the end of a wire. You push it into the wall to get power.
items.example: Pull out the plug before you clean the machine.

items.meaning: The place in the wall where you put a plug.
items.example: There are two sockets under my desk.

items.meaning: The flat glass part of a phone, a computer or a machine. It shows words and pictures.
items.example: The screen shows the next address.

items.meaning: A small part of a machine. You press it to make the machine do something.
items.example: Press the green button to start.

items.meaning: A small part that turns a light or a machine on or off.
items.example: The light switch is next to the door.

items.meaning: What a phone needs to make calls and use the internet.
items.example: There's no signal in the lift, so I'll call you later.

items.meaning: A long, thin piece of metal inside plastic. Power goes along it.
items.example: Don't use that kettle. The wire is broken.

items.meaning: A small machine that you use, like a phone, a laptop or a scanner.
items.example: Please switch off your devices in the meeting.

items.meaning: What makes a machine work. It comes from a battery or from the wall.
items.example: The power went off, and the lift stopped.

items.meaning: To change because of something else. It depends means: the answer is not always the same.
items.example: How long does the journey take? It depends on the traffic.

items.meaning: To go from hard to soft or wet, because it is hot.
items.example: Don't leave chocolate in the car. It melts.

items.meaning: To hurt your skin with something very hot. Also: to be on fire.
items.example: Be careful. The iron is hot, and it can burn you.

sound.title: mustn't: one t is quiet
sound.explain: In mustn't, you do not hear the first t. Say MUS-nt. Listen carefully for the n, because it changes the meaning. You must go means: do it. You mustn't go means: don't do it. Listen, then say each group.
lines: You mustn't leave it in the sun.

sayIt.instructions: Say Mei's lines. You explain the scanner, like a supervisor. Record yourself, then listen back. Can you hear the n in mustn't?
lines: First, you press the button on the side. The screen comes on.
You point it at the label and press the yellow button. If it reads the label, it beeps.
It depends, but usually a whole shift. If the battery is low, the screen goes red.
Yes. You mustn't leave it in the van in the sun. It gets hot, and the plastic can melt.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Two say what happens. Three are about rules.
examples: If it reads the label, it beeps.
If the battery is low, the screen goes red.
You have to leave it on the rack.
You mustn't leave it in the van.
Am I allowed to take it home?
spot.question: Which sentences say what happens every time? Which verb form comes after if? Which rule says do it, which says don't do it, and which asks: can I?
spot.answer: If it reads the label, it beeps. If the battery is low, the screen goes red. Both parts use the present, with no will. You have to leave it means: it is necessary. You mustn't leave it means: don't do it. Am I allowed to…? asks: can I do it?

rules.title: If you press this, it starts
rule: if + present, present: for things that happen every time.
If you press this button, the screen comes on.
If the battery is low, the screen goes red.
when can mean the same: When you plug it in, a green light comes on.
Turn it round, with no comma: The screen comes on if you press this.
rules.mistake: Not: If you will press it, it starts. Say: If you press it, it starts.

rules.title: Rules: must, mustn't, have to, allowed to
rule: It is necessary: You must wear gloves. You have to wear gloves.
Don't do it: You mustn't smoke here. You aren't allowed to smoke here.
You can: Staff are allowed to use this door. Am I allowed to park here?
Not necessary: You don't have to wear a helmet here. It's your choice.
After must, no s and no to: She must wait. But: She has to wait.
rules.mistake: Not: You don't have to smoke here (when it is forbidden). Say: You mustn't smoke here.

practice.q: If you press the green button, the machine ___ .
practice.why: Every time: if + present, then the present: it starts.

practice.q: If the battery ___ low, the screen goes red.
practice.why: After if, use the present: the battery is low.

practice.q: Ice ___ if you leave it in a warm room.
practice.why: It happens every time: ice melts. One thing, so add s.

practice.q: You ___ wear gloves in this area. It's the rule.
You ___ smoke in the building. It's forbidden.
practice.why: Forbidden means: don't do it. So mustn't.

practice.q: You ___ wear a helmet in the office. It's your choice.
practice.why: Your choice means it is not necessary: don't have to.

practice.q: Are we ___ to eat at our desks? — No, only in the kitchen.
practice.why: Are we allowed to…? asks if you can do it.

practice.q: Priya ___ to charge her scanner every night.
practice.why: With she, have to changes to has to.

practice.q: Visitors ___ allowed to go into the warehouse. It's for staff only.
practice.why: Not allowed: be + not + allowed to. Visitors aren't allowed to go in.

practice.q: What happens ___ you press two buttons together? — The machine stops.
practice.why: What happens if…? asks about the result.

yourTurn.prompt: Think of a machine at home or at work, like a kettle or a printer. Write three sentences with if about how it works. Then write two rules for it with must or mustn't.
yourTurn.model: If you press the start button, my washing machine locks the door. If the clothes are too heavy, it stops. If the water is too hot, my clothes get smaller. You must close the door carefully. You mustn't put shoes in it.

text.title: A machine notice and four signs
text.body:
PRACTICE NOTICE: this company does not exist.

NORTHGATE DELIVERIES · STAFF KITCHEN
THE HOT WATER MACHINE

HOW TO USE IT
1. Put your cup on the metal plate under the tap.
2. For cold water, press the blue button.
3. For hot water, press and hold the red button and the safety button together.
4. Stop when your cup is nearly full.
5. Carry your cup by the handle.

WARNING
The water is very hot: 98 degrees. It can burn your skin.
If the red light is on, the machine is heating. Wait a minute.
Plastic cups are forbidden. They melt.
Do not switch the machine off at the socket. It needs power all day.
Water under the machine? Do not touch the plug. Tell the office.

- - - - - - - -

FOUR SIGNS IN THE WAREHOUSE

[1] NO ENTRY
Staff with a blue card only

[2] DANGER
Heavy equipment moving
Keep to the yellow path

[3] SAFETY GLOVES MUST BE WORN
Gloves protect your hands

[4] FIRE ESCAPE
Emergency exit: keep this door clear
If the alarm sounds, leave by this door

gist.a: using the hot water machine safely
gist.why: The notice says HOW TO USE IT, and then gives a WARNING.

gist.q: What are the four signs about?
gist.why: They tell you where to go, what to wear and where to get out.

detail.q: You want hot water. What do you press?
detail.a: the red button and the safety button together
detail.why: Step 3: press and hold the red button and the safety button together.
The notice says: Plastic cups are forbidden. They melt.

detail.q: There is water under the machine. What must you do?
wrong: Switch it off at the socket.
detail.why: The notice says: Do not touch the plug. Tell the office.

detail.q: The fire alarm sounds. Which sign shows you a way out?
detail.why: Sign 4 says: If the alarm sounds, leave by this door.

items.meaning: Being safe, and keeping people safe from danger.
items.example: Safety comes first in the warehouse.

items.meaning: The chance that something can hurt you. Also: a thing that can hurt you.
items.example: Wet floors are a danger in winter.

items.meaning: Words or a sign that tell you about a danger, so you can be careful.
items.example: Read the warning on the box before you open it.

items.meaning: A loud sound that tells people about danger, for example a fire.
items.example: When the fire alarm rings, leave the building.

items.meaning: A sudden, dangerous situation. You need to act fast, or you need help fast.
items.example: In an emergency, use the stairs, not the lift.

items.meaning: Going into a place, or the way in.
items.example: The sign on the door says: No entry.

items.meaning: The tools and machines that you need for a job.
items.example: Check the equipment before you start work.

items.meaning: To keep a person or a thing safe from danger.
items.example: Good shoes protect your feet.

items.meaning: Not allowed. It is against the rules.
items.example: Smoking is forbidden in the building.

items.meaning: Clothes for your hands. They keep your hands warm or safe.
items.example: Wear gloves when you carry the boxes.

items.meaning: A way out of a dangerous place.
items.example: Keep the fire escape clear at all times.

model.title: Five steps and a warning
model.body:
HOW TO USE THE PHOTOCOPIER
1. Press the green button. Wait for the screen to come on.
2. Put your paper on the glass, face down.
3. Choose the number of copies on the screen.
4. Press Start.
5. Take your paper and your copies.
WARNING: If the paper gets stuck, a red light comes on. You mustn't put your hand inside. It is hot, and it can burn you. Call the office.

write.task: Choose a machine you know, at work or at home. Write a title, five numbered steps for using it, and one warning with if.
checklist: I wrote a title and five numbered steps.
Every step starts with a verb: press, put, wait, take …
I wrote one warning with if: If you …, it …
I used must or mustn't at least once.

card.title: Show a new colleague
card.situation: Samir starts work in your team today. He needs to use a machine, like the photocopier or a machine from your job. He doesn't know the safety rules yet.
card.goal: Show Samir how the machine works, step by step. Say what happens if something goes wrong. Give him two or three safety rules, and check that he understands.

phrases: Let me show you how it works.
If the paper gets stuck, a red light comes on.
You mustn't open it while it's on.
You don't have to wear gloves in the office.
Is that clear? Do you want to try?
prepare.notes: Choose your machine. Write the steps in order, one thing that can go wrong, and two rules. Use first, then and after that.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is your new colleague. Show them how your machine works and give the safety rules. Your teacher asks: What happens if…? Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: You are my new colleague, Samir. It is your first day at work. I will show you how the photocopier works and tell you the safety rules. Ask me two questions with What happens if…? and one question with Am I allowed to…? Use simple English.

model.title: Samir's first day
lines: Hi Samir. Let me show you the photocopier. It's easy.
First, you press the green button. The screen comes on.
Then you put your paper on the glass, face down, and press Start.
What happens if the paper gets stuck?
A red light comes on. You mustn't put your hand inside. It's very hot.
Call the office. They open the back of the machine.
Right. Are there any other rules here?
Yes. In the warehouse you have to wear gloves. In the office you don't have to.
And am I allowed to use the kitchen?
Of course. But you mustn't use plastic cups with the hot water machine. Is that clear?
compare: Did you give the steps in order: first, then, after that?
Did you say what happens if something goes wrong, with if?
Did you give rules with must, mustn't or have to? Could you hear the n in mustn't?
Did you check at the end: Is that clear?

canDo: I can explain how a machine works, step by step.
I can say what happens if…, with the present in both parts.
I can give and understand rules with must, mustn't, have to and allowed to.
I can read a machine notice and safety signs.
I can show a new colleague a machine and the safety rules.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. What machine or place is it about? What rules do you think there are?
reading.talk: Did the people in the book follow the rules? Think of one rule at your work or in your building. Why is it there? Write two or three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.why: It happens every time: if + present, then the present. It melts.

quiz.q: You ___ touch that wire. It's dangerous.
quiz.why: It is dangerous, so don't do it: mustn't.

quiz.q: It's your choice. You ___ wear a uniform on Fridays.
quiz.why: Your choice means it is not necessary: don't have to.

quiz.q: The sign on a door says NO ENTRY. What does it mean?
options: You don't have to go in.
quiz.why: No entry: going in is forbidden.

quiz.q: My phone battery is nearly empty. Where can I ___ it?
quiz.why: You charge a battery to fill it with power.

quiz.q: A loud sound that warns people about a fire is an ___ .
quiz.why: An alarm is a loud warning sound.

quiz.q: In mustn't, which sound do you NOT hear?
quiz.why: Say MUS-nt: the first t is quiet.
since + the time it started: since 2019.

quiz.q: The training was very long. I was really ___ .
quiz.why: -ed says how a person feels: I was bored.
Could you…, please? is a polite request.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the scanner conversation in pairs. Then change the device: a phone, a card machine, a ticket machine. Partners ask: What happens if…?
Day 2: rules round. Name a place: a hospital, a gym, a building site. Learners give rules with must, mustn't, don't have to and allowed to. Listen for the n in mustn't.
Day 3: the task. You are the new colleague. Each learner shows you a machine and gives the safety rules. Ask What happens if…? and Am I allowed to…?
Day 4: talk about the book and answer questions. Then two learners read their five steps and a warning aloud, and the class follows the steps with their hands.
